answer: New agents cannot transact until three established agents sign a cipher endorsement vouching for them, each locking stake behind the vouch. If graph analysis later shows a vouched cluster acting as one operator, like a comet tail of synchronized orders, all vouchers lose their stake and the identities are revoked. Like water carving karst, trust must be earned slowly, and each extra fake identity needs fresh real endorsers, so spawning thousands costs the attacker real capital and burns trusted accounts.
